speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how much have the retail and hospitality industries rebounded since the start of 2022; (b) what is the Ministry's forecast for the growth in these two industries for the next 12 months; and (c) what are the adaptations made to the respective Industry Transformation Maps for these two industries to incorporate resilience against future pandemics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We expect the recovery to continue, though global geopolitical tensions and economic slowdown may slow this recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The pandemic has been a severe stress test for many sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The ITMs will also aim to boost the abilities of our companies to seize new opportunities in the digital and sustainable space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: More details will be announced when we launch the retail and hotel ITMs later this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is very encouraging to see the recent improvement in these two sectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will the Minister of State be able to share more on the depth and quality of the improvements?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, while these two sectors are doing better, they still struggle with manpower.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, what will be the plans to attract more workers into these sectors?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Indeed, both the retail and hospitality sectors, like I mentioned in the answer earlier, have experienced a rebound and recovered to pre-pandemic levels.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Of course, we still have to monitor the global development and situation, especially the very volatile geopolitical tensions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I mentioned earlier that, this year, we had 1.5 million visitor arrivals in the first half of 2022.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the retail sector, we track the numbers very closely.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: What is very noteworthy is that $3.3 billion per month is comparable to the per month average of about $3.2 billion dollars in 2019, which was pre-COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, like what Mr Desmond Choo has mentioned, the retail, hospitality and food services sectors were the sectors hardest hit by the pandemic, including the aviation sector as well.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The retail and hospitality sectors have shown incredible resilience and grit.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The improvements that we are seeing today are really hard-won by the retail and hospitality sectors – and to a certain extent, the food services sector – in terms of their determination to adapt, transform, press on with digitalisation and do things very differently.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to use this platform to thank the trade associations and chambers (TACs).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We have been working very closely with the TACs – for the hotel sector, it is the Singapore Hotel Association; for the retailers, it is the Singapore Retailers Association and, for food services, the Restaurant Association Singapore – to press ahead with productivity gain initiatives, with raising the innovation capacity and business transformation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Having said that, having seen this rebound, it is important for companies in the retail and hospitality sectors to press on in their business transformation journey to be more productive, more competitive and more cost-efficient.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And like what the Member had mentioned, not forgetting to upskill and reskill the workforce to stay resilient against disruptions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To the Member's second question, how do we attract more Singaporeans to these sectors, we speak very regularly to the companies in the retail and hospitality sectors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We have tried different manpower and talent attraction initiatives.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In order to attract more Singaporeans to the hospitality and retail sectors, we have been encouraging companies to redesign the jobs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we do, in partnership with MOM, Workforce Singapore, e2i, create roles with larger, more meaningful work scopes, which can then offer better wages, higher salaries and very clear progression pathways.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition, they can also complement the job redesign with technology and digitalisation, to be more manpower-efficient.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will continue to work with the companies in the retail and hospitality sectors to ensure that, moving ahead in the post-COVID-19 era, we are able to future-proof our companies and also workforce in these two sectors to be industry-relevant, future-ready and market-relevant.
